title: Wickens wins Norisring Race 2 as Spengler gives BMW its first podium
dek: Robert Wickens won Race 2 at the Norisring by 7.239 seconds for Mercedes-AMG after passing pole-sitter Bruno Spengler, who recovered to third and gave BMW its first podium of 2015.

chapters.title: Audi’s lead is cut down to size on Saturday
text: Race 1 had reset the story of the weekend. Pascal Wehrlein won the wet-dry Saturday race, Mercedes took the first four places and Audi lost for the first time in 2015 after winning the opening four races. Jamie Green still led the championship on 81 points, but his advantage over Edoardo Mortara and Mattias Ekström had come down to 23 and Wehrlein had climbed to fourth on 57.

For Sunday the question was whether anyone could stop Mercedes and whether BMW, still without a win or a podium, could find anything at all. Sunday’s race was also the longer of the two, scheduled for 60 minutes against Saturday’s 40, so the pit stops would matter more than they had in the rain.

chapters.title: Spengler beats Vietoris by four thousandths to give BMW its first pole
text: Sunday morning’s qualifying produced the closest top three of the weekend. Christian Vietoris and Robert Wickens spent most of the session at the top, and Vietoris began the final minute only 0.009 seconds ahead. Bruno Spengler, a former champion, improved on consecutive laps and put the MTEK BMW #7 on pole with a 48.280, four thousandths of a second faster than Vietoris’ 48.284. It was BMW’s first pole of 2015 and Spengler’s first since the end of 2013.

Wickens set the quickest time in the second sector of his last lap but could not convert it into pole and qualified third on 48.293. He explained that he had not improved on his second set of tyres, which cost him two places. Ekström was fourth on 48.401, the best Audi, ahead of Lucas Auer, Wehrlein and Green, who started seventh. Paul di Resta, Maxime Martin and Daniel Juncadella completed the top ten.
Only 0.625 seconds separated the 24 cars, from Spengler to Miguel Molina on 48.905 in last place, with Timo Scheider 23rd and Marco Wittmann 22nd. Gary Paffett was 11th on 48.516 and Mortara 18th.

chapters.title: A pile-up at Turn 1 and Wickens takes the lead
text: Spengler held the lead into the first corner, but the braking zone behind him was crowded. Maximilian Götz ran into the back of Timo Glock’s BMW, and the chain reaction also took out Augusto Farfus and Mike Rockenfeller. Götz said everyone had braked very late and that he had been hit on the right side shortly before. Glock, Götz, Rockenfeller and Farfus were all out within the first three laps.

At the front Wickens, who had gained a place off the line to run second, was faster than Spengler and sliced down the inside of the BMW at Turn 1 for the lead roughly a quarter of the way into the race. Vietoris then passed Spengler at the chicane and Auer and Ekström followed him through, so that the pole-sitter fell from first to fifth in the space of a single lap.

chapters.title: A quicker stop gives Wickens breathing room
text: Wickens kept Vietoris about half a second behind until the stops, then gained room with a faster stop and managed the gap at around two seconds. Vietoris said he had pulled clear of Ekström earlier in the race but lost a little time to Wickens in the pits.

Further back the stops decided places. Wehrlein, who struggled to overtake in the early laps because the cars ahead were all using DRS and holding each other up, stopped early and found that the tyres needed two laps to come up to temperature. The others stopped right after him and he lost touch. Paffett, who had started 11th, said a slow stop left him behind di Resta with Spengler still further ahead, and he ran out of laps to make up the difference. Auer ran in the leading group in the first half before dropping back.

chapters.title: Spengler passes Ekström to rescue a podium
text: While the Mercedes pair were clear at the front, the interest lay behind them. Spengler spent most of the race behind Ekström, whose Audi was carrying around 30 kilograms more than the BMW, and could not find a way past. The decisive move came at Turn 1 in the closing minute, when Spengler forced his way through. Both drivers described the fight as fair. It gave BMW its first podium of 2015.

Wickens crossed the line 7.239 seconds ahead of Vietoris after 74 laps in 1:01:35.767, and set the fastest lap, a 48.178 on lap 70. Spengler was 10.975 seconds behind the winner and Ekström, the best Audi, 11.595 behind. Wehrlein was fifth, followed by di Resta, Paffett and Juncadella, with Auer ninth and Martin tenth to score the last point. Seven of the eight Mercedes finished in the top nine.
Green, the championship leader, was well down the order and finished a lap behind, outside the points.

chapters.title: Mercedes sweep the weekend while Green’s lead is halved
text: Wickens took his first win of the season and his second at the Norisring, and said he loved the circuit and could not explain why he was always quick there. The Canadian pointed out that, second on Saturday and first on Sunday, he had enjoyed a great weekend, and credited Mercedes with the best car in Nuremberg. Vietoris, fourth on Saturday and second on Sunday, said he was proud of the team even though he had lost a little time to Wickens in the pits. Wehrlein, winner on Saturday, was not fully satisfied with fifth on Sunday: he said an early stop had not paid off because the others came in right behind him.

The weekend belonged to Mercedes. It won both races, took five of the six podium places, saw seven of its eight cars score on Sunday, with Auer collecting his first points. A crowd of 123,000 watched over the weekend. Audi, which had won all four races before Nuremberg, left with Ekström’s fourth place as its best result of Sunday.

For BMW it was a mixed weekend. Spengler’s podium and pole were its first of the year. Spengler himself was delighted but admitted he would have preferred to win, saying the two Mercedes were unbeatable, and BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt praised the pole lap and the fighting spirit that won it the podium. Tom Blomqvist, however, was excluded from the results after the stewards found a driver cooling construction in his car that was not part of its homologation. BMW said the car complied with the regulations and lodged an appeal.

The standings stayed tight. Green kept the lead on 81 points but had seen it cut from 23 to 11, with Ekström second on 70 and Wehrlein third on 67. Mortara was fourth on 58, Wickens fifth on 57 and Paffett sixth on 36. The DTM now has a two-week break before the fourth weekend, at Zandvoort in the Netherlands on 10–12 July.

facts.v: Spengler’s 48.280 beat Vietoris by 0.004 seconds, giving BMW its first pole of 2015 and the first of his own since 2013.
